Imam As-Sajjad ('a) said: Knowledge and the perfect religion is to avoid intruding into unconcerned matters, dispute others rarely, show clemency and steadfastness, and be well-mannered.

Imam As-Sajjad ('a) said: For his supplication (to God), the believer gains one of three things: the supplication is saved for him, he is responded immediately, or he is saved for the befalling of an imminent misfortune.

Imam As-Sajjad ('a) said: Many are those whom are deceived by commendation. Many are those whom are swindled by the firm covering up (of their sins). Many are those whom are trapped by favors and graces that they receive.
Imam As-Sajjad ('a) said: How bad are those whose ones overcome their tens.4 (One good deed will be rewarded tenfold, while bad deeds will be recompensed one for one.)
Imam As-Sajjad ('a) said: God certainly dislikes the stingy that asks others importunately.

Imam As-Sajjad ('a) said: To spend moderately in times of poverty, give generously in times of luxury, treat people fairly, and greet them initiatively—these manners are within the characters of the believers.
Imam As-Sajjad ('a) said: Looks of mutual affection and amiability between the believers is a sort of worship.
Imam As-Sajjad ('a) said: After the acknowledgement of God, nothing is more favorable for Him than moderation in eating and (sexual) chastity. The most favorable act to God is to supplicate to Him.

Imam As-Sajjad ('a) said: All praise be to Him Who has regarded the acknowledgement of His favors as praise. All praise be to Him Who has regarded the acknowledgement of the failure to thank Him properly as showing him gratitude.
Ali Ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Mahbub from Malik Ibn 'Atiyah from Abu Hamza that Ali Ibn al-Husayn (as) said: "There can be no deed (a'mal) without intention (niyyah)."
Muhammad ibn 'Isa has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali who has said the following: "I saw Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.), wearing clothes of lentil color.'"

Hadith.1752 - Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn (as) said: "I have taken a pledge from my Lord (azj), the Mighty and Glorious, that anyone who asks without necessity will one day be compelled by circumstances to beg for a real need."
Hadith.2168 - Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn (as) said: "The one who performs Sa'y between Safa and Marwah is interceded for by the angels, and their intercession is accepted."

147 According to the same documentation, on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Husayn (a.s.), "On the day on which Al-Hassan (a.s.) was born, the Prophet (S) said the general call to prayer (the 'Azan) in his ear."
163 According to the same documentation, it is narrated that whenever Ali ibn Al-Husayn (a.s.) got well after being ill he (a.s.) said, "Enjoy getting cleansed from sins."

Imam al-Baqir.text: Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Use kind words with the hypocrite, love the faithful believer sincerely, and regard your association with (even) the Jew who sits with you.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: The whole perfection is knowledgeability of the religious affairs, steadfastness against misfortunes, and moderation in living.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: By God (I swear), the arrogant is trying to strip God.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: A twenty-year friendship is kinship.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: You would better deal with no one except him whom you did a favor.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Anything of God's act is good for the faithful believer.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: God dislikes people who beg each other importunately, but he loves it for Himself. Hence, God the Glorified likes people to beg Him and ask for what He has in possession.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: People's admonitions will not benefit him whom God does not make him learn lessons of admonition from his own self.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: The scale of him whose outer appearance is more preferable than his conscience is weightless.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: It happens that you address to a man, 'May God fling your enemy,' while that man's only enemy is God.

Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Three categories of people should not say salaam: they are those who are in their ways for offering the (congregational) Friday Prayer, those who walk in a funeral, and those who sit in a public bathroom.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: A scholar whose knowledge is advantageous (for people) is better than seventy thousand worshippers.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: A servant will not be scholar before he gets rid of envying those who precede him and belittling those who are less than him in (grade) of knowledge.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: The need for him who has newly been wealthy is like a dirham in a snake's mouth; you need it but you fear the snake.

Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Deeds without knowledge are not accepted. Knowledge is valueless unless it is matched to deeds. Knowledge guides its bearers to act (good deeds). The deeds of the unknowing persons are worthless.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: You can realize the love that your brother bears for you through the love that you bear for him.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Faith is love and hatred.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Four characters are within the treasures of charity: they are the concealment of neediness, secret almsgiving, suppression of pains, and containment of misfortunes.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: The deeds of the truthful are chaste. The provisions of the well-intended ones are increasable. The ages of those who are benevolent to their wives are addable.

Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Beware of laziness and tedium. They are the keys to every evil. The lazy will not fulfill the rights (that are incumbent upon them) and the tedious will not submit to the right.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Modesty is to accept to sit in a place other than the first row of a session, to greet whomever you meet, and to avoid disputation even if you are right.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: The (faithful) believers are brothers of each other. They should not insult, deprive, or mistrust each other.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said to his son: Submit the right, for he whoever refrains from giving something in its right way will give its two-folds in a wrong way.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Faith will be screened from him who is given idiocy.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Certainly, God hates the speaker of obscene language.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: God punishes physically and mentally, such as harsh livelihood and incapability of worshipping. However, no punishment is harsher than hardheartedness.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: God says: O son of Adam, if you avoid what I have made unlawful, you will be the most pious of people.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: The best adoration is the chastity of the belly and the genitals.

Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Good-humouredness and bright-facedness achieve the others' affection and approaches to God. Bad- humouredness and gloomy-facedness achieve the others' hatred and take away from God.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Pudency and faith are knotted in one bind; whenever one (of them) goes, the other will follow.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: This world is given for the good and the evil, while God dedicates this religion to certain people.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Flattering and envy are not within the faithful believers' traits unless they are used for the sake of seeking studies.

Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Abide by piety, diligence, honesty, and fulfillment of the trusts of the charitable as well as the sinful. If the killer of Ali Ibn Abi Talib ('a) deposits with me a trust, I will surely keep it for him.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: The regard of the relatives purifies the deeds, increases the fortune, refutes the catastrophes, makes the judgment easy, and postpones the death.

Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: God arranges hardships for the faithful servant like the traveler who arranges presents for his people. Likewise, He protects him against the worldly temptations like physicians who protect their patients.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: God gives this worldly pleasure to whom He likes and whom He dislikes equally; but He gives the religion to whom He likes only.
Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Laziness injures both the worldly and the religious affairs.

Imam Al-Baqir ('a) said: Had the beggars realized the reality of beggary, they would not have begged for anything. Had those who do not settle others' needs known the reality of their deed, they would have settled every need.
Through the same chain of narrators it is narrated from abu Ja'far (a.s.) who has said the following: "Whoever has received a share of friendliness has received a share of belief."

It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from his father in a marfu' manner from abu la' far (a.s.) who has said the following: "Abu Ja'far (a.s.) has said, 'No deed with doubt and denial will be of any benefit.'"

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from 'Ammar ibn Marwan from Jabir who has said the following: "Abu Ja'far (a.s.), has said, 'Meeting the Imam is completion of al-Hajj.'"
Aban has narrated from Zurarah ibn 'A'yan who has said the following: "I once asked abu Ja'far (a.s.), about the marriage of a slave-girl. He (the Imam) said, 'No, unless it is an emergency.'"

Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah ibn 'A'yan who has said the following: "I once heard abu Ja'far (a.s.), saying, 'No one other than a father can revoke a marriage.
Ali has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: "Abu Ja'far (a.s.), has said, 'Al-Qur' is the period between two Hayd (menses)."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajj al from Tha'labah from Zurarah who has said the following: "Abu Ja'far (a.s.), has said, 'Al-Qur' is being clean ( Hayd (menses)-free).'"

A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from ibn Mahbub from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: "Abu Ja'far (a.s.), prohibited the use of utensils of gold and silver.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hisham from Zurarah who has said the following: "Abu Ja'far (a.s.), has said, 'Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has created the child of Adam hollow.'"
Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from certain persons of our people who has said the following: "Abu Ja'far (a.s.), has said, 'The master food is meat.'"

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from abu al-Jarud who has said the following: "Abu Ja'far (a.s.), would wear al-Mu'asfar (dye with safflower) clothes and printed clothes."

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from abu Jamilah from Jabir who has said the following: "Abu Ja'far (a.s.), has said that the angels had turbans hanging on them on the day of Badr."

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ibn Khalid from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar who has said the following: "I saw abu Ja'far (a.s.), had applied hair dye with henna of red color.'"

Abu Ali al-Ash'ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from Tha'labah ibn Maymun from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: "Abu Ja'far (a.s.), said, 'Woad has affected my molar teeth. 5 "

Abu Ali al-Ash'ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: "Abu Ja'far (a.s.), has said, 'Applying hair dye with henna stirs up gray hairs.'"
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar who has said the following: "I saw abu Ja'far (a.s.), had applied hair dye with henna.'"

It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from 'Abd Allah ibn Muskan from al-Hassan al-Zayyat who has said the following: "I once saw abu Ja'far (a.s.), had made his beard lighter.'"

It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from certain persons of his people in a marfu' manner has said the following: "Abu Ja'far (a.s.), has said, 'Sweep the house, it removes poverty.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Aban ibn Th'alabah who has narrated the following: "Abu Ja'far (a.s.), has said, 'A part is one-tenth because the mountains were ten and the birds were four.'"
Abaan, from Ali Bin Abdul Aziz, from Abdul Hameed Al-Ta'any, who has said: Abu Ja'far (asws) has said; 'By Allah (azwj)! Had she (asws) spread her (asws) hair, they would have all died'.
(14) Abdul Kareem bin Amr narrated from Thabit bin Shurayh that Abu Baseer had said: I have heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad bin Ali al-Baqir (as) saying: From among us there are twelve inspired ones.

H 329 - Abu Ja'far Ibn Babawayh says: Muhammad Ibn Uthman Amari narrated that by Allah, the Master of this Affair attends the Hajj every year; he sees the people and knows them and they also see him, but don't recognize him.
It has been narrated that Zurarah said "I heard Abu Jafar (a.s) say "In the decree of Allah ﷻ , there is nothing but good for a believer"
It has been reported that Abu Ja'far (a.s) said: When two believers meet and shake hands, Allah puts His Hand in between and it is shaken by the one who loves the other the most.
It has been reported that Abu Ja'far (a.s) said: One who goes a distance to help his Muslim brother until he completes it, Allah will steady his feet on the Day when feet shall waver and slip.
It has been narrated that Abu Ja'far (a.s) said: Feeding four Muslims is equal to freeing a slave from the descendants of Prophet Ishmael.
It has been narrated that Abu Ja'far (a.s) said: (Amongst) the qualities most loved by Allah are three: a Muslim who feeds a hungry Muslim, relieves him from a distress or settle his debt for him.
It has been narrated that Abu Ja'far (a.s) said: Feeding a Muslim is equal to freeing a human being.
Hadith.34 - Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a dead animal that falls into a well. Imam (as) said: "If it has an odor, twenty buckets should be drawn from it."
Hadith.55 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "When a man urinates, he should not touch his private parts with his right hand."
Hadith.56 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "Prolonged sitting in the restroom causes hemorrhoids".
Hadith.86 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "The Commander of the Faithful (as) wiped over his sandals and did not remove the straps".

Hadith.117 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (sw) frequently used siwak (tooth cleaning), but it is not obligatory, so it will not harm you if you leave it for a few days".
Hadith.119 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said about the siwak: "Do not neglect it for more than three days, even if you use it just once."
Hadith.129 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "There is no prayer without purification".
Hadith.277 - Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about dyeing the hair, and He said: "The Messenger of Allah (sw) used to dye, and we still have some of his hair with us."
Hadith.311 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "Whoever trims their nails every Thursday, their child will not suffer from eye ailments".
Hadith.333 - Muhammad ibn Muslim said: "I saw Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) while the barber was trimming his beard, and Imam (as) said: 'Shape it evenly.'

Hadith.344 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "You instruct your deceased to say 'There is no god but Allah (swt)' at the time of death, while we instruct our deceased to say 'Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (sw).'".
Hadith.394 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "Water should not be heated for washing the deceased."
Hadith.400 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "Touching a deceased person at the time of their death and after their washing, and kissing them, is not an issue".
Hadith.458 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), said: "Whoever carries their deceased brother on all four sides of the bier, Allah (swt) will erase forty major sins from them."
Hadith.461 - Abu Ja'far, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), said: "Walking behind the funeral procession is better than walking in front of it, but there is no harm if you walk in front."
Hadith.545 - Imam al-Baqir (as) said: "A mourning gathering (ma'tam) is to be held for the deceased for three days from the day of their death."
Hadith.655 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "The time for Maghrib (evening prayer) begins when the disk of the sun disappears."
Hadith.664 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "A designated angel says, 'Whoever neglects the Isha prayer until the middle of the night, may Allah (swt) never allow his eyes to sleep.'"
Hadith.688 - As for the Mosque of Al-Khayf in Mina, it has been narrated by Jabir from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that He said: "Seven hundred prophets prayed in the Mosque of al-Khayf."
Hadith.717 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "If any of you takes a pebble from the mosque, let them return it to its place or to another mosque, for it glorifies Allah (swt)".

Hadith.732 – Zurarah asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about urine that is present on a rooftop or in a place where one prays. Imam (as) said: "If the sun dries it, then you may pray on it, for it is purified".
Hadith.739 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that He said: "There is no harm in praying on any images (representations) if you place them beneath you."
Hadith.782 - Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as): "Can a man pray while covering his mouth (muffling)?" Imam (as) said: "While on an animal, yes; but on the ground, no".

Hadith.787 – Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that Imam (as) said: "The minimum acceptable covering for you to pray in is to have something on your shoulders, like the wings of a swallow".

Hadith.790 – Zurarah narrated that a man asked him (Abu Ja'far (as)): "If a person sees a scorpion, a snake, or a serpent while he is praying, should he kill it?" Imam (as) said: "Yes, if he wishes to do so."

Hadith.804 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that He said: "There is no issue with praying on mats made from reeds or on palm-leaf mats, and on any plant-based material, except for fruit".

Hadith.853 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "None of you should spit in front of themselves or to their right while praying. Instead, they should spit to their left or beneath their left foot."
Hadith.934 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that He said: "The Qunoot (supplication) is in every two units of both voluntary and obligatory prayers."
Hadith.944 - It is narrated from Zurarah that He said: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir) stated: "All Qunoot (supplication during prayer) is to be recited aloud."

Hadith.1081 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said: "A woman prays in a dress (dir'aa) and a head covering (miqna'a) if it is thick, meaning it is concealing."
Hadith.1090 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said: "When you finish your prayer, turn to your right as you leave."
Hadith.1109 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "Indeed, the truly blind are those who are blind in their hearts, for it is not the eyes that go blind but the hearts within the chests."

Hadith.1324 – Zurarah asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a man performing supererogatory (nafilah) prayers on a ship. Imam (as) said: "He should pray in the direction of its front (bow)."
Hadith.1343 - In the narration from Zurarah from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said: "One who fears robbers should perform their prayer by gesturing while on their mount".
Hadith.1376 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "The time for the night prayer (salat al-layl) is from midnight until its end."

Hadith.1413 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said: "There is Qunoot (a supplication) in every two rak'ahs of the optional (supererogatory) and obligatory prayers."
Hadith.1414 - Zurarah narrated from Him (Imam Abu Ja'far (as)) that He said: "Qunoot (a supplication) is to be recited in all prayers."
Hadith.1456 - Zurarah bin A'yan narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said: "There is no prayer on the day of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha except with a just Imam".
Hadith.1561 - Bukayr ibn A'yan narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that He said: "The Messenger of Allah (sw) never prayed the Duha prayer."
Hadith.1687 - Abu Ja'far (as) said: "Acts of kindness protect against calamities."
Hadith.1690 - Abu Ja'far (as) said: "Everything has a fruit, and the fruit of goodness is hastening to perform it."
Hadith.1729 - Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "Goodness and charity eliminate poverty, increase lifespan, and protect their giver from seventy types of ill-fated deaths."

Hadith.1757 - Imam Abu Ja'far (as) said: "If the one who asks knew what [burden] lies in asking, no one would ask another for anything; and if the giver knew what [reward] lies in giving, no one would refuse anyone."
Hadith.1770 - Abu Ja'far (Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as)) said: "Islam is built upon five things: prayer, almsgiving, pilgrimage, fasting, and wilayah (divinely appointed leadership)."

Hadith.1853 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abu Ja'far (as), who said: "The fasting person is not harmed by what he does as long as he avoids four things: eating, drinking, women, and immersing himself in water."
Hadith.1866 - Al-Ala narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (as), that he was asked about regurgitation (qalas): "Does it invalidate the fast?" Imam (as) said: "No."

Hadith.1873 - Al-Ala narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (as), that he was asked about a man entering the bathhouse while fasting. Imam (as) said: "There is no harm as long as he does not fear weakness."

Hadith.2017 - Zurara and Fudayl narrated from Abu Ja'far (as) who said: "Bathing (ghusl) during the Month of Ramadan should be performed near sunset, just before it, then one should pray and break the fast."
Hadith.2155 - Abu Ja'far (as) said: "Whoever prays two Rak'ahs at the Station of Ibrahim, it is equivalent to freeing six souls."

Hadith.2193 - Abu Ja'far (as) said: "The practice of marking the sacrificial animal (Ish'ar) was deemed good because at the very first drop of its blood that falls, Allah (swt) forgives the person for that act."

Hadith.2226 - Abu Ja'far (as) said: "No servant prioritizes a worldly need over performing Hajj except that they will see the pilgrims who have shaved their heads return before their own need is fulfilled."
Hadith.2266 - Abu Ja'far (as) said: "Honor the pilgrims and those performing Umrah, for this is an obligation upon you."

Hadith.2285 - Zurara narrated from Abu Ja'far (as), who said: "Indeed, Sulayman (as) performed Hajj to the House with the jinn, humans, birds, and winds, and he clothed the Kaaba with garments of fine Egyptian linen (Qibatiyya)."

Hadith.2427 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abu Ja'far (as), who said: "Whoever you associate with, if you are able to ensure that your hand is above theirs (in generosity and giving), then do so."

Hadith.2442 - Abu Ja'far (as) said: "If you travel with someone, travel with your equals, and do not accompany someone who takes care of your needs entirely, for that is a humiliation for the believer."
Hadith.2472 - Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "Everything has a sanctity, and the sanctity of animals lies in their faces."
Hadith.2482 - Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "If you travel through fertile land, proceed gently, and if you travel through barren land, hasten your journey."

Hadith.2543 - Abu Ja'far (as) was asked about a man who performed ghusl for his ihram and then trimmed his nails. Imam (as) replied: "He should wipe them with water and does not need to repeat the ghusl."
Hadith.2598 - It was narrated from Amr ibn Shimmar, from his father, who said: "I saw Abu Ja'far (as) wearing a lightweight striped cloak (burd mukhaffaf) while he was in the state of Ihram."
Hadith.2620 - Abu Basir narrated from Abu Ja'far (as), who said: "I dislike for a Muhrim to sleep on a yellow mattress or a yellow cushion."

Hadith.2648 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abu Ja'far (as), who said: "A Muhrim may apply kohl to his eyes if he wishes, provided it is made with sabr (aloe) and does not contain saffron (za'faran) or turmeric (wars)."

Hadith.2732 - Abu Ja'far (as) passed by a group of people eating locusts and said: "Glory be to Allah (swt)! And you are in the state of ihram?" They said, "It is from the sea." Imam (as) replied: "Then return it to the water."
Hadith.2753 - Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Abu Ja'far (as): "Can a person enter Mecca without being in the state of ihram?" Imam (as) said: "No, except for someone who is ill or has a stomach ailment."
Hadith.2817 - Zurara said: "Sometimes I performed tawaf with Abu Ja'far (as) as he held my hand, completing two or three tawafs. Then he would leave and perform six units of prayer (rak'at)."
Hadith.2963 - Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal narrated from Abu Abdullah (as) regarding a man who enters Ihram for Hajj outside of the months of Hajj. Imam (as) said: "He should make it an Umrah."
Hadith.3018 - In a narration from Ali ibn Atiyyah, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (as), he said: "For the one who fears Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious."
Hadith.3050 - It is narrated by Aban from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (as), who said: "A ram suffices for a man and his household; he may offer it as a sacrifice on their behalf."
Hadith.3060 - Abu Ja'far (as) was asked about an old animal whose front teeth have fallen out. Is it permissible for sacrifice? Imam (as) replied: "There is no harm in sacrificing it."
Hadith.3102 - Abdul Rahman ibn Ayan narrated from Abu Ja'far (as), who said: "A guardian should fast on behalf of a child if the child does not have a sacrificial animal."
Hadith.3138 - Hisham ibn al-Muthanna narrated from Sadeer, who narrated from Abu Ja'far (as), who said to him: "Begin with Mecca and conclude with us."
Hadith.3162 - Jabir narrated from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said: "Part of the completeness of Hajj is meeting the Imam."
Hadith.3229 - It is narrated from Abu Basir that Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad Al-Baqir (as) said: "Whoever judges in a matter of two dirhams and errs has disbelieved."
Hadith.3376 - Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "When the shares are divided, the right of preemption (shufah) is annulled."
Hadith.3534 - Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), said: "The runaway slave's prayer is not accepted until he returns to his master."

Hadith.4030 - Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) was asked about a man who has dirhams or wealth owed to him by another man, and he invites him to his meal or gives him a gift. Imam (as) said: "There is no harm."
Hadith.3613 - Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "Assistance descends from the heavens in proportion to one's needs."

Hadith.3644 - Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "It is written in the Torah that whoever sells land and water, and does not invest its price in land and water, its price will be lost in ruin."
Hadith.3660 - Muhammad bin Muslim asked Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), about a man who prepares medicine for people and takes a fee for it. Imam (as) said: 'There is no harm in it.'
Hadith.4169 - In the narration of Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), he said: "If the blood flows, then eat."

Hadith.4197 - Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), about the meat of horses, beasts of burden, mules, and donkeys. Imam (as) said: "It is permissible, but people find it repugnant."
Hadith.4202 - Aban narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said: "Do not eat the eel (al-jirri) and do not eat the spleen (al-tihal)."
Hadith.4237 - Aban narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said: "Do not eat from vessels made of gold or silver."
Hadith.4300 - Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "No servant leaves something for the sake of Allah (swt), the Almighty and Glorious, and then finds himself in loss because of it."

Hadith.4440 - And Musa ibn Bakr narrated from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said: "A girl should not be consummated with until she reaches nine or ten years of age."

Hadith.4494 - Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about withdrawal (coitus interruptus). Imam (as) said: "The semen belongs to the man; he may direct it wherever he wishes."

Hadith.4620 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said: "Indeed, Allah (swt), the Almighty and Glorious, created desire in ten parts, nine parts in men and one part in women."
Hadith.4677 - Fudayl narrated from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said: "Choose healthy wet nurses, for milk can transmit illness."
Hadith.4939 - Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden alcohol because of its effects and its corruption."
Hadith.5374 - Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a man who forces himself upon a woman. Imam (as) said: "He is to be killed."

Hadith.5521 - Musa ibn Bakr narrated from Zurara from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said: "A girl should not be consummated in marriage until she reaches nine or ten years of age."

Imam al-Sadiq.text: Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: To trust everybody in times of injustice and cheating is disability.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: If problems are added to each other, they will give birth of relief.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: To recognize the actuality of your friend, you should enrage him. If he keeps up his friendship, he is true friend lest, he is false.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Do not appreciate one's affection before you enrage him three times.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Do not trust your friend perfectly, because the knockdown of the trustful is incurable.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Islam is a definite rank. Faith is one rank higher than Islam. Conviction is one rank higher than faith. People have been given a rank lower than conviction.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: To remove a mountain is easier than removing faith.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Faith is in heart and conviction is a number of inspirations.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: The desire for the worldly pleasures causes grief and sadness. Abstinence from the worldly pleasures brings about the rest of both heart and body.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Life is to rent a house and buy bread.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: He who gains oppression is not gaining welfare. He who mistreats people should not complain when people mistreat him.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: In homelands, exchanging visits is the means of association. In travel, correspondence is the means of association.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: A believer is not perfectly virtuous unless he enjoys three characters—knowledgeability of the religious affairs, moderation in living, and steadfastness against misfortunes.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: An actual believer is that whose sexual appetite does not overcome him and whose stomach does not shame him.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: A twenty-year friendship is kinship.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Favors should be done only to the highborn or the religious. Those who show gratitude are very few.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: He who suffers a misfortune due to obtruding upon an unjust ruler will be neither rewarded nor endowed with patience.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: The prosperity of coexistence and association are three thirds: two thirds are acumen and one is overlooking.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Revenging on the pauper is extremely ugly.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) was asked about personality, he answered: Personality stands for that God should not see you in situations against which He warned, and miss you in situations of which He ordered.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: To miss a need is better than asking it from other than its people. Bad mannerism in a misfortune is more catastrophic than the misfortune itself.
As a man asked him a short item of instruction that collects the welfare of this world and the world to come, the Imam, peace be upon him, said: Never tell untruths.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) was asked about eloquence. He answered: Eloquence is to express the idea in as few as possible words. The eloquent is that who attains his demand in the least effort.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Debt is grief at night and humility in day.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: If your worldly demands are attainable, you should check your religion.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Treat your fathers piously so that your sons will treat you piously. Keep yourselves away from the strange women so that your harem will be chaste.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: He who entrusts a betrayer with a deposit will be deprived of God's warranty.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Pudency is of two faces—one is weakness while the other is power, submission, and faith.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Negligence of others' rights is humility. Certainly, the neglector of rights needs for forgery in this regard.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: It is sufficient for one of the groups to salute. Similarly, it is sufficient for one of the groups to respond the salutation.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Salutation is voluntary while responding is obligatory.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Do not answer those who speak before they greet you.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Shaking hands is the perfect greeting of the resident and embracement is the perfect greeting of the traveler.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Shake hands, because this will confiscate malice.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Fear God even if to some extent. Construct a screen between Him and you even if transparent.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Good health is a light grace; it is forgotten when found and mentioned when missed.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: In good days, God endows with the grace of consent. In distress, He endows with the grace of purification.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Everything has limits. The limit of conviction is not to fear anything besides God.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Knowledge is the comrade of the faithful believer, clemency is his supporter, patience is the commander of his army, lenience is his brother, and charity is his father.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: As for those who practice without guidance, they are like him who walks without choosing a definite path. The more he walks, the remoter he becomes.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: He who recognizes God accurately will fear Him. He who fears God accurately will disregard the worldly pleasures.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: The actual fearful is that who cannot speak due to the intensity of fear.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: The firmest handle of faith is to love, hate, give, and deprive—all for God's sake.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: The Divine Throne will be shaken when one makes God the witness of a false matter.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: God knew that sin is better for the believer than self-conceit lest, God will never test the believers through the commitment of sins.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: He whose conducts are bad is tormenting himself.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Nothing like thanks in increasing the favorable matters and nothing like patience in decreasing the unfavorable matters.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: The most effective soldiers of Iblis are women and rage.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: God has not created doubtless conviction more similar to unspoiled doubt than death.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Whenever you see a servant (of God) pursuing people's flaws and neglecting his own flaws, you should then realize that he has been trapped (by the Shaytan).
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: You should not trust the betrayer after you had tested him and you should not accuse him whom you trusted.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: The weary are friendless and the envious are fortuneless. Much looking into wisdom pollinates the mind.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Fear of God is sufficient knowledge and deceit is sufficient ignorance.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: The best adoration is to know God and behave humbly with Him.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: One scholar is better than one thousand worshippers, one thousand ascetics, and one thousand hardworking persons in worship.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Everything has its tax and the tax of knowledge is to teach its people.

Imam As-Sadiq ('a) was asked about the character of decency. He said: The decent is that who turns his sight away from the forbidden views, holds up his tongue from the ill wording, and abstains from oppressing others.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: God will not ask people about things that are screened from them before He identifies them.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: To put your hand to the elbow between the jaws of a dragon is better than asking those who have newly had fortune.

Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: A man's begging from another man is an ordeal: if he gains what he asked for he will then thank the one who did not give him and if he is refuted, he will censure the one who did not refute him.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: God has installed the whole goodness in leniency and courtesy.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Beware of associating with the lowly, because the association with them will never lead to welfare.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: As a man worries about a little humility, this may engage him into a greater one.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: To wear rings on the fingers is a prophetic tradition.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: The most favorable friend to me is that who shows me my flaws.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Comity is one third of the mind.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: The believers' laughter should be only a smile.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: There is no difference between depositing a trust with a betrayer or a negligent.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: He whosever heart is attached to the fondness of this world will be suffering three matters—an everlasting care, an unattainable hope, and an unachievable expectation.

Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Lying and treachery are not within the ethics of the believers. Two characters are not found together in the hypocrites: they are good-looking and understanding of a tradition.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: You should regard him who became angry with you three times without addressing any bad saying to you as a true friend.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: People will live in a time when nothing will be dearer than a good friend and a legally gotten dirham.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: You will not attain the actual faith unless you love the remotest and hate the nearest all for God's sake.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Beware of the two annihilating characters—they are issuing verdicts out of your own opinion and be taking what you do not know as creed.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said to Abu Baseer: O Abu Muhammad, do not spy on people's beliefs lest you will become friendless.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: The gracious forgiveness is to stop punishing for a sin and the gracious patience is that which is empty of complaint.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: He who enjoys veracity, pudency, good mannerism, and gratitude is a faithful believer even if he is fully sinful.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: You will not be faithful believer before you become fearful and hopeful. You will not be fearful and hopeful before you work for what you fear and hope.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Faith is not identified through outer appearances and hopes. Faith is that which is pure in the hearts and assured by deeds.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: If a man is more than thirty-year-old, he is middle-aged. If he is more than forty-year-old, he is old man.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Faith is declaration, practice, and intent. Islam is declaration and practice.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Never break the respect between your friends and you. If respect is broken between you, pudency will vanish. Your amiability will endure as long as there is respect.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: He who puts his friend to shame will be deprived of his relationship with him. He who grieves his friend will lose respect.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Whenever God opens a door to the worldly pleasures, He will open two to acquisitiveness.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: The believer is strange in this world. He should not feel worry of its humility and should not compete with its people for gaining its honor.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: God does not gather good-looking, understandability, and good mannerism for the hypocrites and the corruptive.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Hasty walking removes the believers' brightness and extinguishes their illumination.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: God surely hates the oppressive wealthy man.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Rage eliminates the intelligence of the wise. He who cannot control his rage will not be able to control his mind.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: The niggardly is that who gains wealth illegally and spends it unsuitably.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Muchness of the ill-gotten properties will eradicate the earnings.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Misdemeanor is embittered life.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Richness and dignity are touring. Whenever they notice a place of depending on God, they re-side there.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Good mannerism is a part of the religion. It increases the earnings.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: You should know I will fulfill the trust of even the killer of Ali ('a) if he deposits something with me or seeks my advice or consultation.

Muhammad Ibn Qays said: I asked Abu Abdullah ('a) whether it is acceptable to sell weapon to the two parties both of whom is wrong. He ('a) said: Sell to them only defensive weapons: armors, shields, helmets, and the like.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: God gives the worldly pleasures to those whom He loves as well as those whom He dislikes, while He gives the faith only to whom He selects among the creatures.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: He who declares himself as the leader while there is someone who is more knowledgeable is heresiarch and deviant.

Abu Basseer related: I asked Abu Abdullah ('a) about faith and Islam. He answered: Faith is the avoidance of acts of disobedience to God. Islam is to practice our rites and slaughter animals as we do.

Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: He whosever word of guidance is followed will be gaining the same reward of those who follow it. He whosever word of deviation is followed will be charged of the same punishment of those who follow it.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Piety, openhandedness, steadfastness against misfortunes, and administration of the believers' rights—these four characters are within the ethics of the prophets.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Bad-temperedness, bad humor, envy, obduracy, and oppression—these six characters should never be in the believers' behavior.
The Imam ('a) was asked about the evidence on the existence of the One God. He answered: The evidence is the need of the creatures to Him.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: You will not be regarded as (true) believers before you see the misfortunes as graces and the luxury as disaster.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Hamza (A symbol in the Arabic script representing the glottal stop) is an addition in the Qur'an.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Beware of joking, because it causes rancor and drives into malice. Joking is the lesser revilement.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: If the world advances to some people, it will garb them with the others' charms. If it leaves some people, it usurps their own charms.
Imam As-Sadiq ('a) said: Daughters are advantages and sons are graces. You will be rewarded for the advantages and asked about the graces.

Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about the saying of Allah, "Did We not give you lives long enough so that whoever wanted to be mindful could have done so?" (35:37) So, he said: A rebuke to one who has reached eighteen years of age.
He said: I heard al-Sadiq (as) say: Wellness is a blessing that one cannot duly be thankful for.

It is reported that al-Sadiq (as) said: Yusuf entered prison when he was twelve years old, and he remained in it for eighteen years, and he remained for eighty years after leaving it. That is one hundred and ten years.
And by this isnad. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) said: If one prays five times in congregation in the day and night, then think well of him, and accept his testimony.
And by this isnad, from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father (as) from Jabir b. `Abdullah. He said: Gabriel (as) came to the Prophet (s) and ordered him to take oaths with a witness.
By this isnad. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) said: Lightning does not strike one who is remembering Allah.
By this isnad, he said: Al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) would say: For every people is a government that they draw near to, And our government at the End of Time will manifest.

By this isnad. He said: Al-Sadiq (as) would say: Be steady in your actions, for surely, you will die, Decide for yourself, O human, For it is as though what is past did not occur at all, And what is present is already past.

Mufaddal said: I heard Al-Sadiq (as) say to his companions: He who finds the coolness of our love upon his heart shall increase his supplications for his mother, for surely, she did not betray his father.
Al-Sadiq (as) said to one of his companions: If one of your brethren becomes angry with you three times without saying anything evil about you, then take him as a friend.
Al-Sadiq (as) said to one of his companions: Do not give your brother all your trust, for prudence is unceasing.
Al-Sadiq (as) said to one of his companions: Do not tell a secret to your friend, unless it would not harm you if an enemy were to find out, for a friend can become an enemy one day.
Al-Sadiq (as) said: My father narrated to me from my grandfather (as). Amir al-Mu'minin (s) said: Which of your brothers is perfect? Which man is free of flaws?
Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from 'Isma'il ibn Mihran from one of his people that Abu 'Abdillah (al-Sadiq) (as) said: "Intelligence (al-'Aql) is the guide of a believer."
Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan from Muhammad ibn 'Abdallah from 'Isa ibn 'Abdallah al-'Amri that Abu 'Abdillah (as) said, "Seeking knowledge is obligatory."

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from one of his people that Abu 'Abdillah (al-Sadiq) (as) said: "When a believer who is a Faqih dies, it causes irreparable damage in the Islamic system."

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abdallah has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from abu Ayyub al-Madani from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Husayn al-Ahmasi from abu 'Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. "The heart relies on writing."
Ali has narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Yunus from Hammad from abu 'Abdallah (a.s.) who said: 'I heard him say, "There is nothing except that is has a Book or Sunnah (prophetic tradition)"'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from 'Umar ibn 'Udhaynah from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) who said: "Allah created the Will by itself, then He created all things by the Will."
Ahmad ibn Mihran has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali from al-Husayn Ibn Abu 'Ala' from Abu 'Abdallah (a.s.): I (the narrator) said to him: "Can the earth be without Imam?" The Imam (a.s.) said, "No."

Ahmad has narrated from 'Abd al-'Azim from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from abu 'Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. "The path which leads to Me is a straight (the path of Ali not 'Alayya which means to me)." (15:41)

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, 'Do shake hands, it removes jealousy."

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from 'Abd Allah ibn Al-Mughirah from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) who has said the following: "A councilor cannot lie (is not supposed to)."

It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Sa'id ibn Janah from his brother, Abu 'Amir from a man from Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: "Whoever seeks leadership is destroyed."

A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Mansur ibn al- ' Abbas from ibn Mayyah from his father who has said the following: "I heard Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) saying, 'Whoever wants leadership is destroyed.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) who has said the following: "The Messenger of Allah has said, 'Anger spoils belief just as vinegar spoils honey."
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Yunus from Dawud ibn Farqad who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, 'Anger is the key to all evil.'"

It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Sa'id ibn Janah from his brother abu 'Amir from a man from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) who has said the following: "Whoever has a feeling of self-importance is destroyed."

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) who has said the following: "The Messenger of Allah has said, 'The misfortune for lineage is boastfulness.'"
Yunus has narrated from ibn Muskan from ibn abu Ya'fur who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, 'Whoever publicizes our (confidential) Hadith, Allah will take away his belief.'"

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from 'Anbasah al-'Abid who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, 'If you cannot weep then make a weeping-like face.'"

Mansur has narrated from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) the following: "I heard Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) saying, 'The Messenger of Allah has said, "Complete reading of the Holy Quran is reading to the extent that you know.'"
Ali ibn al-Hakam has narrated from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) who said: "The Quran that Jibril (as) brought to Muhammad (sw) had seventeen thousand verses."

Through the same chain of narrators it is narrated from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) who has said the following: "The Messenger of Allah has said, 'Showing that one loves people is half (the power) of reason.'"
Through the same chain of narrators it is narrated from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) who has said the following: "If one begins speaking before offering the greeting of peace, do not speak to him."

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) who has said the following: ''The Messenger of Allah has said, 'Sneezing is a sign of truthfulness.'"
Ali has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman who has said the following: "Once, I saw Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) sitting in his house near the door facing the Ka'bah."

A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from al-Hassan ibn Kulayb from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) who has said the following: "The laughing of a believing person is smiling."

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, 'Beware of jokes; it takes away the dignity of one's face.'"

Hamid ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Maythami from 'Anbasah al-'Abid who has said that I heard Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) say the following: "Joking is a minor form of name-calling."

Muhammad ibn Yahya in a marfu' manner has narrated the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Water does not become polluted because of the living things which do not have spurting blood when a cut is made in its body.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Wash your clothes because of the urine of inedible animals.'"

Muhammad ibn 'Isma'il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Menopause happens at the age of fifty years."'
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from more than one person who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Camphor is for hunut."

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that the Holy prophet prohibited placing of hunut on a coffin.'"
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from certain persons of his people who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'A shroud is not perfumed"

Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from certain persons of his people from al-Washsha' from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'A deceased is not shrouded in black.'"

Ali has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that the Holy prophet, prohibited digging the grave deeper than three hands (yards)."

Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Uramah from Ali ibn Maysarah from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that a husband is more rightful to place his wife in the grave."

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy from af-Sakuniy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'You must not apply clay to the grave which is not of the clay of that grave.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Yunus from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahab who said: "I once asked abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) about tathweeb in the Adhan and 'Iqamah. He (the Imam) replied, 'It is unknown to us."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from af-Husayn ibn abu Najran from Safwan al-Jammai who has said the foiiowing: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), once led us in al-Maghrib Salah (prayer) and recited al- Ma'udhatayn in two Rak'at."
Muhammad ibn Yahya through the chain of his narrators has narrated who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that it is not desirable to recite all of Chapter 112 in one breath."

Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Ahmad in a marfu' manner has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'If you face uncertainty about Tasbih of Fatimah al- Zahra', 'Alayha al-Salam, say it again.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Yunus from a man who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'There is no confusion (acceptable) in al-Maghrib and morning Salah (prayer)."'

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'I do not see any problem in the rows between the pillars."

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from certain persons of our people who have said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Salah (prayer) is not performed in al-Shuqrah valley.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Yunus from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), disliked to perform Salah (prayer) with clothes that had portraits on them.'"
Muhammad ibn Yahya in a marfu' manner has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Perform Salah (prayer) with your own handkerchief but not with others' handkerchief.'"
Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Wash your clothes clean because of urine of all inedible animals.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ' Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'It is enough sin for one not to provide for his family and lose them.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Having good moral behavior and serving food is part of belief.'"

Muhammad has narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn 'Uthman from Misma' who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that the best charity is cooling off a thirsty liver."

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn ' Atiyyah who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Dawn is when you see it, widthwise, like the whiteness of the suray (canal) (Euphrates river)."'

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'One fasting or while in the state of Ihram must not immerse his head in water.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad who has said the following: "I once asked abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), 'Can a fasting man apply oil to his ears?' He (the Imam) said, 'It is not harmful.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ' Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'It is not harmful if a fasting person swallows his mucus."'

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'If a fasting person is afraid about the illness of his eyes, he is allowed to eat.'"

A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Sindiy from ibn Sinan from a man from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) who said: "Breaking the fast with water washes off sins from the heart."

A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Dawud ibn al-Huseen from abu al-'Abbas who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Without fast 'I'tikaf is not valid.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ' Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'There is no i'tikaaf except with fasting in the general Masjid.'"
A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad in a marfu' manner who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that there is nothing of goodness in neglecting al-Hajj."
A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad who in marfu' manner has narrated who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that gifts are out of the expenses of al-Hajj."

Abu Ali al-Ash'ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd af-Jabbar from Safwan from Dharih who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that the greater al-Hajj is the day of offering sacrifice."
A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from a man who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Awtas is not part of al-'Aqiq.'"
Ali has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Of the Sunnah in Ihram is to trim finger nails, mustache and pubic hairs.'"

Ali has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn 'Isa from Hariz who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Any cloth with which Salat (prayer) is performed is fine to use for Ihram.'"

Ahmad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from 'Abd al-Rahman al-'Arzamiy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'One in the state of Ihram can kill anything whereby one fears for his life.'"

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from in a marfu' manner the following: "About a man who in the state of Ihram eats of the flesh of a prey and does not know what it is, abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'He owes one sheep.'"

Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar has said the following: "I once asked abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), about a man who performs Sa'y between al-Safa' and al-Marwah riding. He (the Imam) said, 'It is not harmful but walking is more virtuous.'"
Aban has narrated from 'Abd al- Rahman who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'In your land a ram is more preferred than al-Jazur (camel)."'

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'It is not harmful to depart in the first chance for departure, then stay in Makkah.'"

Ali has narrated from father, from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that the Messenger of Allah has said, 'You must do Jihad; you will benefit.'"

A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ariy from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Laziness is an enemy of work.'"

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from abu 'Abd Allah al-Barqiy from al-Sarrad who has said the following: "I once said to abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), that I sell arms. He (the Imam) said, 'You must not sell them in times of mischief.'"

Ahmad has narrated from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'The effects of unlawful earning shows up in one's offspring.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Quitting business reduces one's power of reason.'"

It is narrated from the narrator of previous Hadith from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Muyassir who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Selling above fair piece to a believing person is unlawful.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from more than one person who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'It is not a proper weighing until a side of balance tilts.'"

A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Muthanna' from Zurarah who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'One cannot buy or sell an abandoned child that is found.'"

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajjal from Tha'labah from Muhammad ibn Mudarib who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Selling animal dung is not unlawful.'"

Abu Ali al-Ash'ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from ibn Muskan from Yazid ibn Khalifah who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), disliked selling juice for deferred payment."

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hafs al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Settlement by means of mutual agreement is permissible for people.'"
Muhammad ibn Yahya in a marfu' manner has narrated the following: Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that 'Amir al-Mu'minin has said, 'A woman does not give birth before six months/"

Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Durays who has said the following: "I once heard abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), saying, 'Women are given desires of twelve parts and patience of twelve parts.'"

A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from a man who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Proper match is one who is chaste and affluent.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Conduct your marriages during the night and serve food during the day.'"
And Hammad has narrated from Ibrahim ibn abu Yahya who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'The weight of dirham in those days was six.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) who said, 'Breastfeeding does not bring unlawfulness unless it grows flesh and blood.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ' Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Breastfeeding after weaning is not effective/"
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) who said, "The Messenger of Allah (sw) was a father of daughters."
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from abu al-Mighra' from Ali who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, "Aqiqah is obligatory.'"
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Circumcision is of pure obedience to Allah.'"

It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from al-Kahiliy from 'Abd Allah ibn Hilal who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'When they breastfeed for you do not allow them to drink wine.'"
Abu Ali al-Ash'ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Dharih who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'A child is a trial (mischief, attraction)."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Touching women is falling upon them (going to bed with them)."'

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'A pregnant widow does not have any right for maintenance.'"
Aban has narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Whatever of the prey is caught in the snare which is cut off or has died is dead.'"

Abu Ali al-Ash'ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from abu 'Usamah who has said the following: "I once visited abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.). He brought banana nearer to me and I ate.'"

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), disliked using poisonous things for food.'"

Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu'alla' ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha' from Dawud ibn Sarhan who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Do not eat from the utensils of gold and silver.
A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Muhammad ibn Sinan from ibn Muskan from abu Basir who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Overeating is undesirable.'"

Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from al-Husayn, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Do not eat with your left hand if you can.'"

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'A man who looks down on what he has for the guest is ruined.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'The origin of the ruination of body is in ignoring dinner.'"
Al-Sayyariy in a marfu' manner has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that the least of curry is to cut the bread with a knife.'"
Ahmad has narrated from ibn Faddal from af-Mithamiy from abu Basir who has said the foiiowing: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), disliked placing of the loaf of bread under the dish.'"
Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Bakr ibn Muhammad who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, sawiq grows flesh and strengthens the bones .'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ' Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Meat with milk is the sauce of Prophets, 'Alayhim al- Salam. '"

A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from abu Basir who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), liked Zabibiyah (a dish with raisins) quite well.'"
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Tharid is the food of Arabs.'"
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Muhammad ibn Hakim who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that hot food is devoid of blessings.'"
Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Yunus from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Eating fish melts the body.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Vinegar strengthens the power of understanding.'"
Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far in a marfu' manner who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Olives increase in water.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy from af-Sakuniy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that 'Amir al-Mu'minin has said, 'In ghee from cows there is a cure. 5 "

A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu 'Abd Allah from his father from al-Muttalib ibn Ziyad who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Ghee is a very fine sauce.'"

A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Khalid ibn Najih who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Milk is the food of the Messengers."'

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy from af-Sakuniy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that 'Amir al-Mu'minin has said, 'Milk products from cows are medicine."'

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Safwan ibn Yahya from 'Is ibn al-Qasim who has said the following 'I once asked abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), about drinking yogurt water. He (the Imam) said, 'You can drink it.'"
Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu Najran from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Kidney beans dispel gases from the belly.'"
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Al-Sarfan is the master of your dates.'"
A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), disliked the peeling of fruits.'"

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from 'Isma'il ibn Jabir who has said the following: "I once heard abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), saying, The apple is a stomach cleanser.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'If one likes to increase his seed and children he should eat endives very often.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadaqah from Ziyad who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'The endive is the master of herbs.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Drinking water in three breaths is better than in one breath.'"
Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from certain persons of our people in a marfu' manner has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Drinking wine is the key to all evil.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah from a man who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'A wine addict is like a worshipper of idols.'"

It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn Ali from abu Jamilah from abu 'Usamah who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Music (and singing) is the nest of hypocrisy.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Chess is of falsehood.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr in a marfu' manner has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'I dislike to see a man who has received a bounty from Allah but does not show it."

A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from the one who narrated to him who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'It is not unlawful if one has twenty shirts. 5 "

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from a man who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Wearing clothes of sharp color is not desirable except for weddings/"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'The first one who used footgear was Ibrahim 'Alayhi al- Salam."'

A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu 'Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ali from abu al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: "If one wears yellow shoes he continues with happiness until that shoe becomes old.'"

Through the same chain of narrators as that of the previous Hadith the following is narrated: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that Ali, al-Hassan and al-Husayn, 'Alayhim al-Salam, would wear the ring on their left hands.'"

It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from certain persons of his people in a marfu' manner has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Agate is safety on a journey.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Bakr ibn Muhammad who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, 'It is Mustahab (desirable) to use ruby as a ring.'"
A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad in a marfu' manner has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'If one uses a ring of turquoise his palm does not become poor.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ' Umayr from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'It is not unlawful to decorate the sword with gold and silver.'"
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), disliked wearing al-Burtalah (a deep cape)."

A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sa'dan from abu Basir who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'I shave every Friday from this to that duration.'"
It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ibn Faddal from Hammad ibn 'Isa who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Applying eye powder sweetens the mouth.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'It is of the moral discipline of the prophets to brush one's teeth.'"

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Hammad ibn 'Isa who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Tooth brushing stops tears and sharpens eyesight.'"
Sahl in a marfu' manner has narrated the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'A man must not enter a bathhouse with his son to allow him look at his private parts.'"

A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from a man from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd who has said the following: "I once heard abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), saying, 'I like al-Khuluq."'
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Applying oil demonstrates wealth.'"
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Viola oil is the master of your oils.'"

Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), once said, 'From your area no other thing comes more likable to us than viola.'"
Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from in a marfu' manner the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'Sweet basil is of twenty-one kinds and the master among them is myrtle.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, 'Everything has honor. The honor of animals is in their faces.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from certain persons of his people who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'The saddle is a condemned riding thing for women."'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu'alla' ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha' from Ishaq ibn Ja'far who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), once said to me, 'Son, keep sheep but do not keep camels.'"

Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn Mahbub from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: "I once asked abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), about marking the animals. He (the Imam) said, 'It is not harmful except their faces.'"

A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad in a marfu' manner has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, with pigeons, keeps a house safe from crumbling down.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'It is detestable for a Muslim to allow a dog to live in his house."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ' Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has narrated the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'The shroud is paid for from the whole of the legacy."'

Yunus has narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr who has narrated the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said testimony of women about virginity and every defect which men cannot look at is admissible.'"
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ' Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has narrated the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said that the oath can be turned to the plaintiff."

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has narrated the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'A binding oath which is false leaves the town barren.'"

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ' Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has narrated the following: "Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s.), has said, 'A man must not be asked to take an oath except for what he knows.'"
