Ali has narrated from his father from 'Abdillah Ibn al-Mughira from Abi al-Sabbah that Abu Ja'far (al-Jawad) (as) said: "Passing a sleepless night due to an illness is more rewarding than a whole year worshipping."
Hadith.2734 - Abu Ja'far al-Thani, Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (as) said: "Slaughtering the game, eating it, and paying the expiation is more beloved to me than eating carrion."

Imam al-Hadi.text: Imam Al-Hadi ('a) said to one of his adherents: In a friendly manner, blame (somebody) and say to him: When God intends goodness for somebody, He makes him accept the blame of the friends.
Imam Al-Hadi ('a) said: There are definite places in which God likes the servants to supplicate to Him. One of these places is the tomb of Al-Husayn; master of the martyrs ('a).
Imam Al-Hadi ('a) said: The thankful of a grace should be happy for thankfulness more than it is for the grace.

Imam Al-Hadi ('a) said: The clement oppressor is about to be acquitted for his clemency, while the foolish rightful one is about to extinguish the illumination of his right with the blows of his foolishness.
Imam Al-Hadi ('a) said: You should present thorough obedience to those who present for you their thorough love and advice.
Imam Al-Hadi ('a) said: Do not feel secure from those who disgraced their personalities.
Hadith.424 - Abu Al-Hasan al-Thalith, Imam Ali ibn Muhammad Al-Hadi (as) was asked whether musk and incense (bukhoor) should be brought near the deceased. Imam (as) replied: "Yes."

Imam al-Askari.text: Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: Do not dispute (with others) lest you will lose splendor and do not joke (with everyone) lest you will be disrespected.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: As for those who accept to sit in a place other than the first row of a session, God and His angels will bless them until they leave that session.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: Within the unforgivable sins are the sins whose committers wish if they would not commit any-thing else.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: To greet everyone, you pass by and to sit in a place other than the first class of a session are signs of modesty.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: Reasonless laughter is a sign of ignorance.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: Within the misfortunes that deal a death blow is the neighbor who overshadows any good feature that he notices and propagandizes any defect that he notices.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: Very much offering of prayers and fasting is not the worship; the very worship is the very much pondering over the affairs of God.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: Anger is the key to every evil.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: The least comfortable of people is the spiteful.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: The faithful believer is a blessing for the believers and a claim against the disbelievers.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: The guaranteed sustenance should not engage you from the ordained deed.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: The powerful will be definitely humiliated if he ignores the right and the humble will be definitely valued if he takes in it.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: Fatigue is the friend of the ignorant.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: Nothing is above two characters: believing in God and benefiting the friends.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: The babies who dare their fathers will surely treat them impiously when they attain maturity.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: To show happiness before the grieved is not a sign of good mannerism.

Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: Everything that you dislike your life if you lose it is surely preferred to your life, and everything that you desire for death if it befalls you is surely eviler than death.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: To educate an ignorant and to prevent a habit are two impossible actions.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: Modesty is an unenviable favor.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: Do not bestow upon anyone with matters that are difficult for him.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: Those who advice their friends secretly are respecting them, and those who advice them openly are humiliating them.
Imam Al-Askari ('a) said: God's favors encompass every misfortune.

Sayyida Fatima.text: Ja'far, from Anbasat, from Abu Abdullah (asws) having said: 'Beware of mentioning Ali (asws) and Fatima (sa) (in front of others) for there is nothing more hateful to them than the speaking of Ali (asws) and Fatima (sa)'.

Imam al-Mahdi.text: (47) Ali bin Abu Hamza narrated from Abu Baseer that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: "One of the signs that precedes the appearance of al-Mahdi will be the eclipse of the sun in the middle of Ramadan."
